title: Uniform product expectation bound
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $P$ be a finite set, and let $m$ be a natural number. For each $p\in P$, choose a set $D_p\subseteq\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$, and suppose each coordinate belongs to exactly two of these sets. Let $g_p$ be a nonnegative real-valued function of assignments $a:\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\to\Omega$ that depends only on the coordinates in $D_p$. When the coordinates of $a$ are chosen independently and uniformly from $\Omega$, the expectation of $\prod_{p\in P}g_p(a)$ is at most $\prod_{p\in P}\sqrt{\mathbb E[g_p(a)^2]}$.
hypotheses_covered: Each coordinate belongs to exactly two sets $D_p$
Each $g_p$ is nonnegative on every assignment
Each $g_p$ depends only on coordinates in $D_p$
Assignments are uniformly distributed over all maps from the coordinate set to $\Omega$
